back_translation: I will sing a song for my beloved, a song of my beloved concerning his vineyard: My beloved had a vineyard on an exceedingly fertile hill.

He dug the soil all through and cleared out the stones, then planted choice-breed vines. He built a tower in the middle of the vineyard and also hewed out a winepress in it. Then he watched in hope for it to produce good grapes, but it produced rotten grapes instead.
"And now, O inhabitants of Jerusalem and men of Judah, judge between me and my vineyard.
What more was there to do for my vineyard that I have not done for it? When I watched in hope for it to produce good grapes, why did it produce rotten grapes?
Now I will tell you what I am about to do to my vineyard: I will tear out its thorn-hedge, and it will be devoured; I will break down its wall, and it will be trampled.
I will turn it into a wasteland, with no pruning and no hoeing, and briers and thornbushes will spring up. And I will command the clouds not to pour rain upon it."

For the vineyard of the LORD of Hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah are the planting He delighted in. He watched in hope for justice, but behold — bloodshed instead; He watched in hope for righteousness, but behold — a cry of distress instead.
Woe to those who join house onto house and attach field to field until no open space remains, and you must dwell alone in the midst of the land.
The LORD of Hosts spoke so that I heard it with my ears: "Surely many great houses will become desolate; beautiful mansions will have no occupant.
For ten yokes of vineyard will yield only one bath of wine, and a homer of seed will yield only an ephah of grain."
Woe to those who get up at early dawn to chase after strong drink, who dawdle on into the late night until wine inflames them.
At their banquets there are lyre and harp, tambourine, flute, and wine — but they pay no attention to the royal deeds of the LORD and do not see the work of His hands.
Therefore my people must go into captivity for lack of knowledge; their honored men go hungry, and their multitude is parched with thirst.

Therefore the realm of the dead enlarges its throat and opens its mouth wide beyond measure; the dignity of Zion and her multitude, with her noisy throng and the revelers within her, will plunge down into it.
Mankind will be pressed down low, and the people made to fall low, and the eyes of the haughty will be brought down low.
But the LORD of Hosts will be held in exaltation through justice, and the holy God will display His holiness through righteousness.
Then lambs will graze as if in their own pasture, and kids and sheep will feed among the ruins of the rich.
Woe to those who drag iniquity along with ropes of deceit, and haul sin as if with a cart-tethering rope,
those who say, "Let Him hurry, let Him speed up His royal work so that we may see it! Let the plan of the Holy One of Israel draw near and arrive so that we may know it!"
Woe to those who call evil good and call good evil, who take darkness for light and light for darkness, who take bitter for sweet and sweet for bitter.
Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes and shrewd in their own opinion.
Woe to those who are heroes — at drinking wine, and mighty champions — at mixing strong drink,
who let the guilty go free for the sake of a bribe, and strip the innocent of the justice that is theirs.

Therefore, as a tongue of flame devours the stubble, and as dry grass sinks down into the blaze, so their root will rot and their blossom will blow up like dust — because they have rejected the law of the LORD of Hosts and have despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.

Therefore the wrath of the LORD blazes against His people; His hand is stretched out against them and strikes them down. The mountains quake, and their corpses are like refuse in the middle of the streets. Even so, His wrath has not turned back, and His hand is still stretched out.
He will raise a signal flag for the distant nations and whistle with His lips to call them from the end of the earth — and behold, they come with urgent speed.
Not one of them grows weary or stumbles; no one slumbers or sleeps. No belt at their waist comes loose, and not a single sandal strap is broken.
Their arrows are razor-sharp, and all their bows are bent ready; the hooves of their horses are like flint, and their chariot wheels like a whirlwind.
Their roar is like a great lion; they roar like young lions; they growl and pounce on the prey, then drag it away with no one able to rescue it.
In that day they will roar over their prey like the roaring of the sea. And when one looks at the land — behold, darkness and anguish; even the light is blotted dark by its thick clouds.
